title: KeyHunter Operation: Harvard Alumni Data, Stanford Applications and LLM Key Theft
content_md: The KeyHunter Operation pairs LLM key theft with an academic fraud campaign that reaches Harvard alumni data, Stanford applications and 18 other universities. SOCRadar’s Threat Research Unit (STRU) attributes the operation to leepsmarts, a Chinese-speaking threat actor, with activity confirmed as late as October 13, 2026. The operation runs on two main tracks: theft of LLM API credentials from misconfigured cloud infrastructure, and an academic fraud campaign targeting 20 institutions, 19 of them in the US. Both run on infrastructure in China, South Korea, Malaysia and the US, are coordinated through AI agent frameworks (Hermes Agent, OpenClaw), and are managed from a custom dashboard on the actor’s primary server. LLM Key Theft 2,233 API keys harvested Keys from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and DeepSeek 12 marked valid by the actor’s own tooling 247 exposed LLM gateways catalogued, serving models from these providers and Meta Academic Fraud 20 Institutions targeted, 19 in the US 195 Harvard alumni records from a torrent-distributed dataset tied to the November 2025 ShinyHunters incident Application payment links for Stanford, UChicago, Wake Forest, Case Western and Central Michigan Accounts created at NY
